back: The breakdown of rock in its original place by physical, chemical or biological processes, without transport.
The downslope movement of soil and rock under gravity, e.g. soil creep, landslides, mudflows, rockfalls.
Outer layers of rock expand by day and contract at night (and are released from pressure), so curved sheets peel off. Common with a large daily temperature range.
Chemical weathering in which water reacts with feldspar in granite to form clay, so the rock rots; quartz remains as sand.
Rainwater absorbs carbon dioxide to form weak carbonic acid, which dissolves limestone and dolomite.
Joints guide deep chemical weathering underground; corestones survive where joints are wide apart; the regolith is stripped away, exposing a pile of boulders.
A large, bare, smooth granite dome with few joints, e.g. Domboshava.
Stalactite: calcite column hanging from a cave roof. Stalagmite: column growing up from the floor. Joined: a pillar.
Cyclone Idai (March 2019): heavy rain triggered landslides and debris flows in Chimanimani and Chipinge districts.
Hazard mapping and zoning, replanting vegetation, drainage, terraces, retaining walls and gabions, early warning and education.
